title: Platform systems & services: integrated runbook, dashboards, alerts, and roadmap
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the platform engineering systems and services runbook, the primary dashboards and alert thresholds we operate against, retrospective findings from Q4 2025 - 1Q1 2026, and the near-term roadmap for reliability and observability. It is intended as the single-entry reference for on-call, platform engineers, and owners planning changes to monitoring or architecture.

Audience
- On-call engineers
- Platform and SRE teams
- Product/infra engineers making changes to platform services

Owner and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-platform (engineering)
- Runbook author: Priya Nair (Platform Engineering)
- On-call escalation: PagerDuty policy "Platform-Oncall" (policy id: PD-PLAT-01)
- Slack channel: #platform-ops

High-level SLOs and targets
- API request latency (p95): <= 120 ms (hosted control plane endpoints)
- Inference request tail latency (p99): <= 500 ms (production fleet)
- Control-plane availability: 99.95% monthly
- Alert-to-acknowledge median: <= 90 seconds (on-call target)

Systems & services inventory (summary)
- control-plane-api: handles user routing, model catalog, and policy checks. Owner: API team.
- scheduler: orchestrates job placement on Dedicated pools. Owner: infra-scheduler.
- serving-proxy: ingress for inference requests, performs auth and routing. Owner: serving-runtime.
- kv-cache-service: Redis/managed cache for KV and prefix caching. Owner: serving-runtime.
- metrics-ingest: Prometheus remote-write + Cortex cluster for long-term metrics. Owner: observability.

Primary dashboards (Grafana)
1) Platform Overview (dashboard id: PLAT-OV-01)
   - KPIs: control-plane success rate, API latency p50/p95/p99, active customers, error budget burn rate.
2) Serving Runtime Health (SR-HEALTH-02)
   - KPIs: host GPU utilization, queue length per pool, avg tokens/sec, KV cache hit rate, model-variant fallbacks.
3) Autoscaler & Capacity (AS-CAP-03)
   - KPIs: pending pods, scale events, time-to-scale, failed scale attempts.
4) Cost & Throttling (COST-04)
   - KPIs: tokens / USD, throttled request rate, per-tenant throttles.

Alerting matrix (high-level)
- Sev 1 (pager oncall): control-plane down (>= 5m error rate > 50%), serving-proxy 5xx surge (> 10% error rate sustained 3m), circuit-breaker triggered for > 3 model variants, total cluster GPU OOM events > 1/m.
- Sev 2 (oncall slack + email): p95 latency breach for control-plane (> 200ms sustained 10m), queue length per pool > 5x normal baseline, kv-cache hitrate < 60% for 5m.
- Sev 3 (email): slow leak in metrics ingest (missing 10% of series over 60m), sustained increase in cost per token (+20% vs baseline over 24h).

Alert definitions (examples)
- control_plane_5xx_rate_pct > 10 for 3m
- serving_proxy_5xx_rate_pct > 10 for 3m AND traffic_volume > 100 rps
- gpu_utilization_avg > 95% for 15m in a single pool
- kv_cache_hit_rate < 60% for 5m
- slo_error_budget_burn_rate > 10 over 1h

Runbook: common incident playbooks
1) Control plane degraded (5xx spike)
   - Step 1: Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and post incident stub to #platform-ops with current metrics link. (Owner: on-call)
   - Step 2: Confirm scope: run quick checks on control-plane-api upstream dependencies (auth, DB, k8s API). Commands:
     - kubectl -n control-plane get pods --selector=app=control-plane-api
     - curl -v https://control-plane/api/health
   - Step 3: If DB appears degraded (latency or errors), page DB team and apply read-only failover if configured. Otherwise proceed to restart the failing replicas using rolling restart (kubectl rollout restart).
   - Step 4: If root cause is deployment (new release): roll back to previous revision: kubectl rollout undo deployment/control-plane-api --to-revision=<previous>. Follow with post-incident release-block checklist.
   - Step 5: Postmortem: create incident in Jira ticket type "Incident" and link to this doc. Complete RCA within 5 business days.

2) Serving runtime tail latency spike
   - Step 1: Verify whether spike is global or pool-specific. Check Serving Runtime Health dashboard.
   - Step 2: If queue depth is high, enable emergency autoscale override (if policy exists) or increase pool capacity via infra console. Command: curl -X POST https://infra-api/scale -d '{"pool":"<pool>","delta":+2}' (replace with internal cli).
   - Step 3: Check for model-variant fallbacks in the last 5m; if many fallbacks, identify model version causing regressions and route traffic to last-known-good variant. Update routing rule: POST /routing/override.
   - Step 4: If GPU OOMs observed, reduce max batch size for the model variant and re-evaluate.

3) KV cache degradation (low hit rate)
   - Step 1: Confirm backend Redis availability (redis-cli --cluster info).
   - Step 2: If nodes unhealthy, promote replica or perform rolling-restart per Redis runbook.
   - Step 3: If hit rate dropped due to a cache key eviction storm, temporarily enable aggressive caching policy for hot prefixes and notify product about workload change.

Escalation matrix
- Oncall -> Senior Platform Engineer (if unresolved after 20 minutes) -> Platform Lead (if unresolved after 60 minutes) -> CTO (if customer-impacting > 2 hours).

Operational procedures and checklists
- Daily (on-call handoff) checklist:
  1) Review Platform Overview dashboard for any active alerts.
  2) Confirm there are no active rollouts in last 30 minutes.
  3) Verify backup jobs for control-plane DB completed in last 24h.

- Weekly maintenance (run by infra-scheduler):
  - Capacity forecast run and autoscaler policy tuning (document changes in changelog).
  - Cache eviction and compaction job validation.

Configuration snippets (alert rules)
- Example Prometheus alert rule (YAML):
  - alert: ControlPlane5xxSpike
    expr: sum(rate(control_plane_http_errors_total[3m])) / sum(rate(control_plane_http_requests_total[3m])) * 100 > 10
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "Control plane 5xx rate > 10%"

- Example Cortex config entry for retention: retention_days: 365

Logging and traces
- Trace sampling: 100% for control-plane (first minute of incident window), 10% for serving runtime baseline.
- Key log fields: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, backend_node_id, cache_hit

Post-incident retrospective (Q4 2025 - 1Q1 2026 highlights)
- Summary of incidents:
  - 2025-12-03: Control-plane deployment caused 5xx spike for 17m. Root cause: incompatible middleware version. Action: enforce pre-deploy integration test and add canary rule. (Owner: API team)
  - 2026-01-18: Serving runtime tail latency due to sudden load from customer X. Root cause: missing per-tenant throttling. Action: implement per-tenant rate-limits and burst controls. (Owner: platform)
  - 2026-02-10: Redis eviction storm causing KV cache hit rate drop. Root cause: unbounded key growth from new eval harness. Action: add per-namespace quotas and synthetic load tests. (Owner: serving-runtime)

- Retrospective action items (status)
  1) Add pre-deploy canary gate for control-plane APIs (in progress, ETA 2026-03-15) — Owner: API team.
  2) Implement per-tenant throttling (in progress, ETA 2026-04-01) — Owner: platform.
  3) Enforce cache quotas and add eviction alerts (done) — Owner: serving-runtime.
  4) Improve oncall runbook clarity and add runbook links in alert annotations (done) — Owner: eng-platform.

Roadmap (next 6 months)
- Sprint Q2 2026:
  - Deliver per-tenant throttling and burst controls (priority 1).
  - Launch read-only control-plane fallback in a secondary region (priority 2).
  - Observability: Migrate metrics ingest to Cortex v1.8 for better cardinality handling (priority 1).
- Sprint Q3 2026:
  - Autoscaler improvements: predictive scaling based on token-rate trends.
  - Integrated chaos testing for serving runtime to validate graceful degradation.

Change management & runbook updates
- Any change to alert thresholds, dashboard queries, or runbook steps must be documented in this page and submitted as a PR to the platform-runbook repo. Major threshold changes (>= 20% change) require sign-off from the SRE lead and one other reviewer.

How-to: add an alert with runbook link
1) Create/update Prometheus rule in infra-monitoring repo.
2) Include an annotation runbook_url: <this page link> in the rule.
3) Open PR with description, impact, test plan, and at least one reviewer from observability.
4) After merge, update the related_pages list above with the rule file path.
